messages:
Ravi: Heads-up: milestone planning sync. We hit two blockers that force a decision: the prompt-store performance regressed on long tails, and the new routing policy needs infra work. Do we reset timeline or reprioritize?
Maya: Given customer commitments, prefer trimming prompt-store features (search, fuzzy ranking) to v1 and keep core prompt save/load for MVP. Routing infra feels higher risk to cut; reliability is higher priority.
Ellen: If we trim prompt-store we must communicate to early adopters and give a toggle. Also update docs so partners don't depend on fuzzy search.
Jake: Agree on toggle. Also propose a micro-milestone: freeze infra changes for 2 weeks and only land critical routing fixes. That limits fallout.
Ravi: How about a two-lane milestone board: Lane A = Launchable MVP (core inference, basic prompt store, routing safeguards), Lane B = v1 (prompt-store advanced, routing perf tuning, analytics). We'll aim MVP in T+3 weeks, v1 in T+10.
Maya: T+3 seems aggressive if we still need canary stability. Suggest T+4 weeks but with a hard feature cut deadline in 5 days to lock scope.
Ellen: Communication plan: publish a "what's in MVP" note and a short customer FAQ. I'll draft it and share by EOD.
Jake: Operational gating: define three go/no-go checks before candidate: 1) canary p99 < 900ms for 24h, 2) error_rate < 0.5% on canary, 3) successful rollback tested in staging.
Ravi: Good. Add a fourth: docs + feature-flag in place. If any fail, we reset to T+2 weeks for mitigation and re-run checks.
Maya: Action items: Maya -> produce updated schedule and adjust milestone board (due in 48h). Ellen -> draft customer-facing MVP note + FAQ (EOD). Jake -> add gating checks to release playbook and run a rollback drill (3 days). Ravi -> notify sales and set expectation for pilot customers.
ci-bot: Release ticket created: PROD-3141. Canary job scheduled pending gating checks.
Ravi: If no objections, I'll lock the plan and move non-blocking features to the v1 lane.
